faq: Can existing users keep their accounts?
Yes. If your backend already holds accounts, the iOS app signs in against it. If accounts live only inside the old app, we plan the data move first. Standard and Premium carry data over.
Do you rebuild the app pixel for pixel?
We match features and brand, but follow iOS habits for navigation, buttons and gestures. An iOS app should feel native, so some screens look different from Android or web, by design.
Can purchases made on Android transfer to iOS?
No. Apple and Google keep purchases separate, so subscribers must be matched through your own accounts or restored by login. We can set up account-based access to help where store rules allow it.
What do you need to start?
Source code or a working build of the current product, API details and any design files you have. We need access to your Apple Developer account later for TestFlight. No passwords are needed.
desc:
iOS app migration from Android, web or Objective-C brings your product to iPhone in modern Swift. Ecom Swift LLC plans what must carry over, rebuilds the app natively, connects your existing data and prepares the release in your own Apple account.

## What is iOS app migration?

iOS app migration is the move of an existing product onto the iPhone platform. There are two common cases. In the first, you have an Android app or a website and want a native iOS version of it. In the second, you have an older iOS app written in Objective-C, and you want it moved to Swift and SwiftUI so it is easier to maintain.

In both cases the goal is the same: keep what users already value, and build it the way iPhone users expect.

## Why migrations need a plan first

A migration is not a copy and paste. Android and iOS differ in navigation, permissions, notifications, purchases and design habits. A web app has no concept of a home screen icon, background tasks or a system share sheet. An old Objective-C app may hide years of business rules inside code nobody remembers.

Starting without a plan leads to missing features, lost data and users who feel the new app is a different product. A written list of what moves, what changes and what is dropped prevents most of these surprises.

## How a good migration affects your business

For a company with a strong Android or web product, an iOS version reaches a new group of customers without redesigning the service. For an owner of an old iOS app, a move to Swift lowers the cost of the next feature, because current developers can read and change the code.

Existing users matter too. If accounts, saved items and purchases carry over, nobody has to start again, and the change is welcome rather than disruptive.

## What a careful migration includes

- A feature list that separates must-have, nice-to-have and retired items.
- A map of your data model, so each record has a clear home in the new app.
- Connection to your existing API, rather than a second backend.
- Account login that works for current users.
- Native iOS navigation, controls and gestures, not a copy of another platform.
- Push notifications moved to Apple's notification service.
- Subscriptions and purchases rebuilt with StoreKit where the app sells digital content.
- Testing on several iOS versions and screen sizes through TestFlight.
- A store listing and screenshots for the new version, where the package includes it.

## How we work

We begin by studying your current product: the screens, the data and the rules behind them. Then we write the migration plan, with the feature list and the order of work. After you approve it, we rebuild the core screens in Swift, connect the API and test with real accounts.

Basic gives you the written plan plus the first core screens built in Swift. Standard builds a working iOS version of the core product with login, existing data and notifications. Premium covers a fuller rebuild with purchases, tested data migration, a store listing and submission support.

You test each build through TestFlight, and we adjust as you give feedback.

## Moving from Objective-C to Swift

When an older iOS app is the starting point, we usually move it in stages rather than in one jump. New screens are written in SwiftUI, while stable parts can stay until they are replaced. This keeps the app shipping while the code improves, and it avoids a long freeze with no releases.

## Purchases across platforms

Purchases made on Android or on the web are tied to those stores. Apple does not transfer them. We can help you design a way to recognize existing customers, for example through accounts on your own backend, while following App Review Guidelines. The right choice depends on what you sell, and we explain the options before building.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which features must be in the first iOS release.
- Provide an API that the iOS app can use.
- Test with accounts that have large amounts of old data.
- Accept that the iOS version should feel like an iPhone app.
- Keep your brand elements consistent across platforms.

**Avoid:**
- Demanding a pixel-for-pixel copy of another platform.
- Migrating every rarely used feature on the first release.
- Ignoring how Apple handles digital purchases.
- Switching the backend and the app at the same time.
- Retiring the old app before the new one is stable.

## Who this is for

A company with an Android app that now wants iPhone customers is the most common buyer. A business with a mobile website that has outgrown it, and an owner of an older Objective-C app that no developer wants to touch, also fit well.

## What we need from you

Send a link or build of your current product, any source code you can share, your API documentation and your brand files. We work in your own Apple Developer account as a team member and in your repository as a collaborator. We never need passwords. A short list of the users and data that must carry over helps us begin.
